referenceRoles.A: Current city v5 is the camera-correction edit target; chapter 1 harbor is a high-view/style reference
referenceRoles.B_C: New high-view residential A fixes roof/side-wall ratio; each old v5 segment supplies its distinct lot layout

A.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Production portrait game-map texture, opaque 1024x1536.
Image 1 is the CURRENT CITY MAP and the EDIT TARGET. Image 2 is the first-chapter high overhead painting used only to guide aerial framing and broad clean materials. Keep a modern abandoned urban street, not a coast.
Primary correction: RAISE THE VIEWPOINT substantially, to a HIGH BIRD'S-EYE VIEW approximately 75-80 degrees above the horizontal ground, only 10-15 degrees off straight down. Redraw the architecture with that one consistent high orthographic camera. Image 1 is too oblique and shows whole tall facades: do NOT preserve that camera. The new map must be immediately recognizable as high overhead, while still showing a little building height.
Visible building surface should be roughly 80-85 percent roof and 15-20 percent narrow foreshortened side face. Roofs are broad readable planar shapes; a facade is a SHORT STRIP underneath or beside the roof, no more than about one sixth to one fifth of that roof's projected depth. Show a small amount of compressed wall/window/door/awning detail, not a full-height multi-storey elevation. NO tall fronts with five or six clearly stacked window rows. Keep side walls present; do NOT produce a pure satellite roof-only view, floor plan or totally flat diagram.
Preserve the useful overall street route, varied building setbacks, modern rectangular architecture, connected forecourts and sidewalks, restrained ruin corners, street trees and quiet middle flight corridor. Preserve the clear painted material finish: pale sunlit roof planes, blue-gray shaded narrow walls, slate asphalt, controlled green clumps, no all-over dirty microtexture. Adjust physical footprints and occlusion correctly for the raised camera instead of squashing the old image.
Maintain a single sunlight direction from upper right. Credible building and tree shadows fall lower left ON the same continuous street/paving surface, with tight wall-foot contact, so the buildings remain grounded. At this high camera angle the shadows may convey more height than the narrow visible facade. Keep shadow shapes readable but moderate in contrast for bullet visibility; never outline each block with a dark halo.
No bright platform perimeter, extruded sidewalk skirt, floating building island, detached isometric stickers, paper cutouts, diorama, separate asset-sheet objects or vanished contact. A few restrained road markings and crosswalks connect street and paving. All structures, ground and shadows must share the new high aerial camera, no mixed projections.
Maintain low open street-connection ground at the top and bottom 10%, with no tall roof, wall or long shadow cut by the tile edges. Keep quiet matching asphalt endpoint values for a scrolling companion set. No clouds, fog, aircraft, actors, enemies, parked or moving vehicles, projectiles, pickup icons, UI, text, logos, watermark, transparent regions or extra panels.
This is the residential/service segment A. Output ONE full-frame finished map, not a camera-angle comparison sheet.

B.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Production opaque portrait game-map texture 1024x1536.
Image roles: image 1 is the APPROVED HIGH BIRD'S-EYE city segment A: match its camera, roof-to-wall proportions, clean dimensional material treatment, slate road, sun direction and integrated ground shadows. Image 2 is the old oblique city segment that must be RE-DRAWN from that raised camera; retain its distinct building types and broad street/yard arrangement, not its old facade proportions.
Use a high orthographic aerial camera approximately 75-80 degrees above the ground, 10-15 degrees off straight down. Roof surfaces should dominate approximately 80-85% of visible building area, while a narrow foreshortened side face and small compressed window/entrance details remain visible. Match image 1 exactly on this balance. A side face is a short band no more than roughly one fifth of its roof's projected depth; NO tall fronts with five or six visible stacked window rows. Do not go fully vertical or produce roof-only satellite blocks: preserve visible side-wall volume, a little window/awning detail, contacts and height.
Reproject the whole scene consistently. Keep modern rectangular architecture, flat roofs, varied setbacks, connected pavement/forecourts, ordinary service entrances, controlled healthy olive-green clumps and some local damaged corners. No medieval arches, vaulted windows, floating platforms, thick bright perimeter, paper cutout silhouettes or independent pasted isometric assets.
Light from upper right; buildings and trees cast coherent grounded shadows toward lower left, onto the same road and pavements. Right-side shadows must visibly anchor to footprints and overlap subdued road paint or paving joints. Keep shadows moderate and broad enough for quiet bullet contrast; no dark outline halos. Clean pale sunlit roofs and blue-gray shaded short walls, no all-over dirty grunge or microcracks.
Preserve a continuous quiet central flight corridor, roughly the middle 40%, with low-contrast asphalt/patches and restrained markings. Thin ordinary curbs and flush cuts join road and paving. Top/bottom 10% must be low quiet open cross-street ground, matching image 1's endpoint position and asphalt values, with no tall roof/wall or long shadow sliced by the edge.
No clouds, fog, aircraft, actors, moving or parked vehicles, enemies, projectiles, UI, text, logos, watermark, transparency or comparison panels. ONE finished texture.
Segment B: ordinary office/commercial buildings, a recessed delivery alley and a locally collapsed corner; keep the camera high and show roofs with short sides.
